column3: Close to the Greek; “break” is rendered “transgress.”
NKJV adds “to God” after “a gift” and expands the clause to “whatever profit you might have received from me.”
NKJV includes “or mother” and reads “the commandment of God,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “his father” and reads “the word of God.”
NKJV includes “draw near to Me with their mouth,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “honor Me with their lips.”
Close to the Greek; “pit” is rendered “ditch.”
NKJV names “Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “He said.”
NKJV has “not yet,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Do you not understand.” “Is cast out into the sewer” is rendered “is eliminated.”
Close to the Greek; “sexual immorality” is rendered “fornications” and “slanders” as “blasphemies.”
Close to the Greek; “right” is rendered “good,” and the diminutive “dogs” as “little dogs.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV has “Jesus' feet,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “His feet.”
